author: felicepantaleo
body:
The truth graph holds the full history of a simulated event. PR #51716 added truth levels to it. A level is a named rule that decides which particles count as truth objects. Examples are the particles that reach the calorimeter, or the hadrons that carry a b quark. A level never holds a particle together with one of its own ancestors, so the same energy is never counted twice. This PR adds the layer that compares reconstruction against those truth objects, and the DQM package that plots the result.

Any efficiency or fake rate needs one decision first: which truth object should a given reconstructed object correspond to. This PR answers that question with detector hits. A truth object owns the simulated hits of its particle and of every descendant of that particle. A reconstructed object owns the hits or the clusters that built it. The association compares the two sets of hits and gives a score in each direction. One score says how much of the reconstructed object the truth object explains. The other score says how much of the truth object the reconstructed object recovers.

The harder question is which truth object to compare with, and the answer depends on the event. Take a neutral pion that decays to two photons. If the two photons stay separate in the detector, the right truth objects are the two photons. If reconstruction merges them into one object, then no single photon explains that object, and the right truth object is the pion. A fixed choice of level is therefore wrong for one of the two cases.

This PR resolves that with an adaptive search. The search starts at the truth object that matches directly. It then moves up the decay chain while the larger truth object still explains the reconstructed object, and it stops where the match is best. In the example above it stops at the photon in the first case and at the pion in the second case. Each reconstructed object gets its own answer.

The search is exposed as working points. `Fixed` does not move up the chain at all. `AdaptiveTight` and `AdaptiveNominal` allow a small and a larger amount of climbing. One property makes these working points easy to interpret: a working point changes which truth object an object matches, never whether it matches at all. The set of reconstructed objects with a match is therefore the same at every working point. The fake rate does not move, and any change in purity measures the truth definition alone.

The PR provides these associations for tracks, tracksters, primary vertices and secondary vertices. For each input collection it writes one reconstruction-to-truth map per working point, and one truth-to-reconstruction map. A shared producer computes the truth targets once per event, so the cost does not grow with the number of associator modules. Nothing runs by default: a customise function wires the modules for the jobs that want them.

The DQM package turns those maps into the standard plots. For every collection, every truth level and every working point it books the efficiency, the purity, the fake rate, and the rates of duplicated and merged objects, against transverse momentum, pseudorapidity, energy and the size of the truth object. Because the truth level is an axis rather than a fixed choice, the same job answers the same question at several definitions of truth, and the plots can be read side by side. This is also what makes the association layer reviewable: an efficiency that moves when only the truth definition changes is visible immediately.

The PR also repairs two defects in code that #51716 merged. That PR removed the truncation parameters from the two graph dumpers but left the parameters in the configurations, so those modules fail parameter validation today. More important, a cycle in the graph could empty a truth level in silence, because the rule that removes covered members lets a member of a cycle remove itself. An empty level looks exactly like an event with no such particle, so the code now detects a cycle and reports it. Two smaller fixes prevent an index from wrapping past the end of a hit array, and stop the dumper from reporting energies against the wrong hits when an input collection is absent.

### Validation

The measured numbers below each state their sample.

The adaptive search works as intended on tracks. On 200 TenTau events without pileup, the purity of the truth match rises from 0.34 at `Fixed` to 0.86 at `AdaptiveNominal`, while the fake rate stays the same, as the construction requires. The whole associator chain costs 0.89 s per event on ttbar at PU200, measured on 10 events; the shared target producer costs 12.5 ms of that.

The truth side was verified on ten generator presets, with one sample per preset and 10 events per sample, on Run4 D122. The presets cover particle guns, single resonances, vector boson fusion, gluon fusion, top pairs, single top, dibosons, associated Higgs production, heavy flavour and inclusive QCD. Across 103 event graphs, every stored level bit agrees with a fresh recomputation, and the graph shows no cycle, no orphan fragment and no particle with more than one production vertex. A separate script reads the published graph files and repeats the check with its own code: no level ever holds a particle and one of its ancestors, a subgraph always holds at least the hits and the energy of the particle itself, and no neutrino carries hits.

The physics numbers are correct sample by sample. Top pair events give two b hadrons and two top quarks. Associated Higgs production gives two b hadrons from the H to bb decay, and single top gives one. Vector boson fusion gives six hard-process legs, which are the two tagging quarks and the four neutrinos, and no b hadron. Higgs to two photons gives two hard-process legs. Inclusive QCD names no resonance, so it has no signal level, and it still has 351 reconstructable final-state objects per event.

One caveat on the heavy-flavour sample. The standard `BsToMuMu` fragment states a filter efficiency of 1.38e-3, so ten accepted events are too expensive for this campaign. The heavy-flavour preset was therefore verified on the top-pair sample, where it seeds on hadron flavour and finds the expected b hadrons. The preset is verified; that particular fragment is not.

The branch builds on its own and passes all nine unit test suites. The DQM configuration constructs its 26 modules and sequences in a job.

### Notes

The DQM package is included here rather than in a later PR, because the association maps and the truth targets have no other consumer, and a reviewer cannot judge the association layer without seeing what it plots.

Energy sums and scores use `double` deliberately. The sums of squares span keV squared to TeV squared, and the reverse score subtracts two large and nearly equal terms. Quantities that do not accumulate use `float`.

Some commits change code that #51716 merged rather than the new association layer. They are here because one configuration fails today and the level defect is silent.
title: Truth Graph: branch association library and reco-to-truth associators
